pr.title: Rename dump of coroutine by-move-body to be more consistent, fix ICE in dump_mir
pr.description:
First, we add a missing match for `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody` in `dump_mir`. Fixes #129703. The second commit (directly below) serves as a test.

Second, we reorder the `dump_mir` in `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` to be *after* we adjust the body source, and change the disambiguator so it reads more like any other MIR body. This also serves as a test for the ICE, since we're dumping the MIR of a body with `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody`.

Third, we change the parenting of the synthetic MIR body to have the *coroutine-closure* (i.e. async closure) as its parent, so we don't have long strings of `{closure#0}-{closure#0}-{closure#0}`.

pr.author: compiler-errors

processing.reason: The PR is a compiler-internal MIR dumping/diagnostic fix, not a miscompilation. Its observed effects are (1) avoiding an ICE in dump_mir by classifying DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody as function-like, (2) moving the dump after `by_move_body.source` is set to the synthetic def id, and (3) changing the synthetic def's parent so the pretty-printed symbol path is `{closure#1}` instead of a nested `{closure#0}-{closure#0}-{closure#0}` chain. The accompanying async-closure test changes only dump file names/tags and snapshot text; the concrete async-closure program's runtime behavior is unchanged. Therefore there is no historical wrong transformation of program values that can be represented as two ordinary Rust functions with identical inputs/signatures whose defined Miri executions return different numeric/boolean/character values. Encoding the name/depth difference or the dump ICE as a synthetic return value would manufacture a semantic difference not present in the PR, which the task explicitly forbids.

analysis.summary: In StateTransform's by-move coroutine body construction, dump_mir must recognize DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody as a function-like body or MIR dumping ICEs. The fix adds that DefKind to write_mir_sig's is_function match, moves the dump after by_move_body.source is reset to the synthetic def id, and parents the synthetic body to parent_def_id so its name is a single `{closure#1}` rather than a nested `{closure#0}-{closure#0}-{closure#0}` chain. Test expectations move to `built.after.mir` and emit both synthetic body variants.
analysis.originalLogic: When building a by-move coroutine body, `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` clones the coroutine body, applies MakeByMoveBody, creates a synthetic def (`DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody`) and sets `by_move_body.source` to that synthetic def id. MIR dumping (`dump_mir` -> `write_mir_sig`) classifies a body as a function only for `DefKind::Fn | DefKind::AssocFn | DefKind::Ctor(..)`; otherwise it falls back to `tcx.is_closure_like(def_id)`. The synthetic body's parent/def-id creation also determines the pretty-printed symbol path.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically the synthetic by-move body's `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody` was not matched in `write_mir_sig`'s is_function test, so dumping MIR of that body (made visible by moving the dump after the source is changed to the synthetic def id) hit the closure-like fallback and ICE'd (issue #129703). The synthetic def was also created under `coroutine_def_id`, producing deeply nested names like `{closure#0}-{closure#0}-{closure#0}`. Correct behavior: add `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody` to the function-like match, parent the synthetic body to `parent_def_id` so it is `{closure#1}` ("This will always be `{closure#1}`, since the original coroutine is `{closure#0}`."), and dump with tag `built`/`after` after the source update.
analysis.inputDomain: Async closures / coroutine closures whose call shim needs a by-move coroutine body (e.g. calling an `AsyncFn`/`AsyncFnMut`/`AsyncFnOnce` through `&`, `&mut`, and by value), compiled with MIR dumping enabled (`-Zdump-mir`) and possibly under both panic strategies.
analysis.trigger: Dumping MIR of a MIR body whose `source.def_id()` has `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody`, especially after `by_move_body.source` has been set to the synthetic def id.
preconditions: A by-move coroutine body is synthesized in StateTransform (coroutine_by_move_body_def_id).
The synthetic body is assigned DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody.
dump_mir is enabled for the body, with the dump placed after the body source is adjusted to the synthetic def id.
write_mir_sig must classify the synthetic body as function-like rather than relying on is_closure_like.
pitfalls: Dumping before updating by_move_body.source can hide the synthetic-DefKind ICE; the dump location relative to source mutation matters.
The closure-like fallback in write_mir_sig is not a valid substitute for explicitly matching DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody.
Choosing coroutine_def_id as the synthetic body's parent creates long nested `{closure#0}` chains and unstable-looking dump names; use the coroutine-closure parent_def_id.

Test expectations must be renamed/updated for the new `built.after` dump tag and for emitting both by-move body instances; merely keeping the old coroutine_by_move snapshot does not test the new behavior.
Do not infer execution or reproduction from the snapshot diff; no compiler was built.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a mir-opt test with `// skip-filecheck` and EMIT_MIR entries for the async-closure by-move bodies. Exercise `call(&async_closure)`, `call_mut(&mut async_closure)`, and `call_once(async_closure)` to generate both by-ref/by-move shims. Emit `main-{closure#0}-{closure#0}-{closure#0}.built.after.mir` and `main-{closure#0}-{closure#0}-{closure#1}.built.after.mir` (and the analogous `{closure#1}` variants) to pin the synthetic-parent naming, and remove `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY` so the dump no longer needs per-panic duplicates. Verify the header reads `// MIR for ... after built` and the function name shows the single `{closure#1}` synthetic body.

Second, we reorder the `dump_mir` in `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` to be *after* we adjust the body source
Third, we change the parenting of the synthetic MIR body to have the *coroutine-closure* (i.e. async closure) as its parent, so we don't have long strings of `{closure#0}-{closure#0}-{closure#0}`.
